questions.q: What does lowering a SiK's AIR_SPEED from 64 to 16 kbit/s give you?
options: Nothing: only transmitter power sets the range
About 6 dB and roughly twice the range
Lower latency in the control link
questions.explain: Sensitivity improves by ~3 dB for every halving; 6 dB is twice the range.

questions.q: Which parameters must match on a SiK pair?
options: Only SERIAL_SPEED and TXPOWER on both radios
NETID, AIR_SPEED, ECC, frequencies and channels
questions.explain: Otherwise the radios will not link; SERIAL_SPEED is the UART speed on each radio's own side.

questions.q: What is the SiK parameter MAVLINK = 1 for?
options: Switching the radio to the old MAVLink 1 protocol
Giving the video stream priority over telemetry
questions.explain: The radio frames packets on MAVLink boundaries and injects RADIO_STATUS; ArduPilot adjusts its streams by txbuf.

questions.q: RSSI = 190, noise = 60. The fade margin is roughly?
How much does range grow with +12 dB of margin?
questions.explain: Every 6 dB doubles it: 12 dB is ×4.

questions.q: Why is ECC on SiK not recommended?
options: It halves the useful throughput; some chips lack it
Radio rules forbid it in many countries
It needs a separate wire to the flight controller
questions.explain: Golay coding doubles the transmitted data; some newer radio chips do not support it and do not work with ECC = 1.

questions.q: What is an IP radio/mesh for, rather than SiK?
options: The cheapest and simplest telemetry for 1–2 km
Video, SSH and several aircraft on one network
questions.explain: An IP radio is an Ethernet bridge: MAVLink over UDP, video, access to the companion computer, a fleet.

questions.q: The main risk of LTE telemetry?
options: MAVLink cannot be sent over IP
Very short range in a city
questions.explain: You need a VPN or a relay and a mandatory link-loss failsafe.
